_meta.scope: Tier-B published methods identified from IP's OPEN-TEXT user-program / formula sources. IP's own built-in Module algorithms ship compiled (UserProgram.dll per module); those are identified by module name + manifest + published-method inference and flagged compiled_boundary=true. Nothing was decompiled. SandiBumi reimplements every method from the cited PRIMARY paper, never from IP.
_meta.calibration_note: Mirrors Techlog D_python_algorithms.md. KEY CONTRAST: Techlog shipped its high-value kernels compiled (.pyc/.dll); IP ships the user-program SDK EXAMPLES as readable source in 7 languages (VB/C#/C/FORTRAN/MATLAB/Python x2), but IP's proprietary built-in Modules are equally compiled. So the readable-vs-compiled boundary in IP falls between 'SDK examples' (open) and 'shipped Modules' (compiled).

readable_tierB_methods.capability: Hydraulic Flow Units - permeability from porosity by rock-type/HFU cluster
readable_tierB_methods.published_method: Amaefule et al. hydraulic (flow) units + RQI/FZI; plus Winland r35 and Pittman apex-radius permeability transforms
primary_citations: Amaefule, Altunbay, Tiab, Kersey, Keelan (1993) SPE 26436 - 'Enhanced Reservoir Description: Using Core and Log Data to Identify Hydraulic Flow Units and Predict Permeability in Uncored Intervals/Wells'
Kolodzie (1980) SPE 9382 / Winland r35 (unpublished Amoco, via Kolodzie)
Pittman (1992) AAPG Bulletin 76, 'Relationship of Porosity and Permeability to Various Parameters Derived from Mercury Injection-Capillary Pressure Curves for Sandstone'

formulas_as_read.RQI_FZI: perm = phi^3 * ( FZI / (0.0314 * (1 - phi)) )^2   [inverted Kozeny-Carman; 0.0314 = um unit constant; RQI=0.0314*sqrt(k/phi), phiz=phi/(1-phi), FZI=RQI/phiz]
formulas_as_read.Winland: log10(k) = ( log10(r35) - 0.732 + 0.864*log10(phi*100) ) / 0.588   [rearranged Winland: log r35 = 0.732 + 0.588 log k - 0.864 log(phi%)]
formulas_as_read.Pittman: log10(k) = ( log10(rXX) - C[i,0] + C[i,2]*log10(phi*100) ) / C[i,1]   [Pittman apex rXX: log rXX = a + b log k + c log(phi%); a,b,c = Pittman.Constants[i,0..2], per rXX percentile]

constants.pittman_constant_table: Pittman.Constants[rXXindex,0..2] is COMPILED in the DLL (not readable). SandiBumi should take a,b,c from Pittman (1992) published Table for r10..r75.
constants.coefficient_source: per-HFU coefficient (mean FZI / target r35 / target rXX) supplied via data.xml, one per HFU number; can be overridden by Monte Carlo

readable_tierB_methods.model_switch: Model text param in {RQI, Winland, Pittman}; PittmanIndex selects rXX percentile row
readable_tierB_methods.sandibumi_action: Reimplement RQI/FZI directly from SPE 26436 (trivial algebra). Winland/Pittman from AAPG 1992 with the published coefficient tables.
readable_tierB_methods.scope: v1-core (permeability + rock typing feed net-pay and SCAL integration)

readable_tierB_methods.file: C:\Program Files\IP2025\UserPrograms\Interp_Demo\UsersCode.py (identical logic in .cs/.vb/.c/.f/.m; report defaults in 'Interp Demo C Report.txt')
readable_tierB_methods.capability: Complete deterministic quicklook openhole interpretation (Vcl -> porosity -> Sw -> BVW -> net-pay/net-res cutoffs -> zonal averages) with interactive Pickett-plot m/Rw back-solve
readable_tierB_methods.published_method: Standard openhole petrophysics: linear GR-index Vcl; Wyllie sonic / density porosity with clay correction; Archie OR Indonesia (Poupon-Leveaux) Sw; optional Shell variable-m; Pickett (1973) crossplot inversion
primary_citations: Poupon & Leveaux (1971) SPWLA - 'Evaluation of Water Saturation in Shaly Formations' (Indonesia equation)
Wyllie, Gregory & Gardner (1956) - sonic time-average porosity
Pickett (1973) - resistivity-porosity crossplot for m and Rw
Shell / Nigeria variable cementation: m = 1.87 + 0.019/phi (Shell empirical, Gulf-Coast/Niger delta unconsolidated sands)

formulas_as_read.porosity_sonic: phi = (DT - DTma) * Cp / (DTfl - DTma)   ; clay term PorClay = (DTclay-DTma)*Cp/(DTfl-DTma)
formulas_as_read.porosity_density: phi = (RHOB - RHOma) / (RHOfl - RHOma) ; clay term PorClay = (RHOclay-RHOma)/(RHOfl-RHOma)
formulas_as_read.pickett_backsolve: m = (log10(Ro1) - log10(Ro2)) / (log10(phi2) - log10(phi1)) ; Rw = Ro1 * phi1^m / a (clamped 1e-4..100)

readable_tierB_methods.sandibumi_action: SandiBumi already has all of these (memory: Archie/Simandoux/Indonesia switch, Vsh methods, Wyllie/density porosity). Value is confirming IP defaults match SandiBumi and the Pickett-plot->code back-solve UX pattern.
